narrator.brief: A man in his late fifties, a warm, resonant baritone with a storyteller's intimacy. Unhurried and even, as if reading aloud by lamplight to people he loves; reverent without being pompous or sing-song. Every word clear, never rushed, and steady enough to listen to for hours.
narrator.inspiration: The great narrators of recorded Bibles were mature, cultured voices that never upstaged the story: Michael York (The Word of Promise), John Rhys-Davies (Truth & Life), Orson Welles narrating King of Kings (1961), and the classic single-voice KJV readers.
narrator.scripture: Carries about half of all the words in the Bible; must stay pleasant over 70+ hours.

God.brief: An ageless male voice of overwhelming majesty: a vast, resonant bass that seems to fill a great space, rich, full and powerful, every word weighty and sure. Slow, deliberate and commanding, the voice of the one who made heaven and earth; grand without strain, sovereign and utterly certain, with deep warmth beneath the power. Tender in mercy, terrible in judgment.
brief_history: 2026-10-09, before the owner asked for 'grander': An ageless male voice, deep and immense yet quiet: a low bass-baritone with great warmth and stillness. Slow and deliberate, never shouting; authority that needs no force. Tender in mercy, terrible in judgment, intimate when calling a prophet by name. No theatrical boom.
God.inspiration: Productions have gone two ways: the vast, deep voice (Martin Jarvis in The Word of Promise, Brian Cox in Truth & Life, Samuel L. Jackson in The Bible Experience) and the intimate one (the burning bush in The Prince of Egypt). We want both in one: depth without bombast.
God.scripture: A still small voice (1 Kings 19:12); speaks with Moses face to face, as a man speaketh unto his friend (Exodus 33:11). About a fifth of all the words in the Bible, mostly the prophets' oracles.

Paul.brief: A wiry man in his fifties, an intense, slightly reedy baritone. Rapid, driving reasoning that piles clause on clause; passionate and persuasive, sometimes sharp, deeply tender with friends. A scholar's precision, a traveller's weariness, and no grandiose oratory.
Paul.inspiration: Stacy Keach (The Word of Promise), James Faulkner (Paul, Apostle of Christ). The text suggests a brilliant writer who was not an impressive speaker.
Paul.scripture: His letters are weighty and powerful; but his bodily presence is weak, and his speech contemptible (2 Corinthians 10:10).

Jesus.brief: A man of about thirty-three, a warm, clear baritone with quiet authority. Approachable and kind, speaking to people rather than at them; natural rhythm, never pious or sing-song. Capable of fierce rebuke, playful irony and broken grief, but always the same person.
Jesus.inspiration: The most loved portrayals are human and present rather than stately: Jonathan Roumie (The Chosen), Robert Powell's intense calm (Jesus of Nazareth), Jim Caviezel (The Word of Promise, The Passion of the Christ), Neal McDonough (Truth & Life), Blair Underwood (The Bible Experience).
Jesus.scripture: The common people heard him gladly (Mark 12:37); he taught them as one having authority (Matthew 7:29).

Moses.brief: An old man, eighty and beyond: a weathered, gravelly baritone with a slightly heavy, deliberate tongue, choosing his words carefully. Meek and patient as a shepherd, but immovable, and capable of blazing anger. Grows in authority from the hesitant man at the bush to the farewell orator of Deuteronomy.
Moses.inspiration: Charlton Heston's commanding Moses (The Ten Commandments), Ben Kingsley (Moses, 1995), Richard Dreyfuss (The Word of Promise), Forest Whitaker (The Bible Experience), Val Kilmer and Christian Bale in film. We take the age and gravity, and add the halting speech the text gives him.
Moses.scripture: I am slow of speech, and of a slow tongue (Exodus 4:10); the man Moses was very meek (Numbers 12:3); eighty years old when he spoke to Pharaoh (Exodus 7:7).

John.brief: The beloved disciple, from his twenties to great age: a gentle, intimate, warm tenor-baritone, contemplative and loving; the voice of an old man remembering, when he writes.
John.inspiration: George Xanthis (The Chosen); Louis Gossett Jr. voiced John in The Word of Promise, whose cast includes the writers of the books.
John.scripture: That disciple whom Jesus loved (John 21:7); Little children, love one another (1 John).

Solomon, king.brief: A regal man in his forties, a smooth, cultivated, articulate baritone. Measured and aphoristic, every sentence balanced; poised and assured, with a later world-weary, reflective melancholy.
Solomon, king.inspiration: Yul Brynner (Solomon and Sheba) and Malcolm McDowell (The Word of Promise) played him polished and kingly.
Solomon, king.scripture: A wise and an understanding heart (1 Kings 3:12); Vanity of vanities (Ecclesiastes 1:2).

Jeremiah.brief: A man in his thirties to forties, a tenor-baritone with an earnest, aching quality. Urgent and anguished, tears close to the surface; reluctant, sensitive, but burning with a message he cannot hold in.
Jeremiah.inspiration: The weeping prophet is usually played as young and fragile rather than stern.
Jeremiah.scripture: I am a child (Jeremiah 1:6); his word was in mine heart as a burning fire shut up in my bones (Jeremiah 20:9); Oh that mine eyes were a fountain of tears (Jeremiah 9:1).

David.brief: A man in his thirties, a bright, lyrical baritone with a musician's phrasing. Passionate and quick to feel: exuberant joy, fierce courage, raw repentance. A warrior-poet's energy, charismatic and warm.
David.inspiration: Gregory Peck (David and Bathsheba), Gary Sinise (The Word of Promise), Michael Iskander as the young David (House of David).
David.scripture: Ruddy, of a beautiful countenance (1 Samuel 16:12); cunning in playing, a mighty valiant man, prudent in matters (1 Samuel 16:18). 'David (old)' uses this voice, older and frailer.

Job.brief: A man of about sixty, a rich baritone worn rough by suffering. Eloquent, dignified, poetic; raw grief and anguished protest that never loses its nobility. Long sentences delivered with a broken man's stubborn clarity.
Job.inspiration: Audio dramatizations treat Job as a great tragic role for a classical actor: the speeches are poetry and need a voice that can carry them.
Job.scripture: Perfect and upright (Job 1:1); I will speak in the anguish of my spirit (Job 7:11).

Jacob (Israel).brief: A man whose life runs from quick, clever youth to great age: a soft-spoken, persuasive tenor-baritone, smooth and careful, a schemer's quickness that mellows into a patriarch's weary tenderness.
Jacob (Israel).inspiration: Played as Esau's opposite: the quiet, calculating brother (Joseph: King of Dreams gave the old Jacob a tender, grieving voice).
Jacob (Israel).scripture: The voice is Jacob's voice, but the hands are the hands of Esau (Genesis 27:22): Jacob's voice must be unmistakably different from Esau's.

Isaiah.brief: A man in his prime, a majestic orator: rich, resonant baritone with poetic grandeur and an aristocrat's polish. Soaring in comfort, thunderous in rebuke.
Isaiah.inspiration: The most literary of the prophets; productions give him a classical actor's voice.
Isaiah.scripture: Here am I; send me (Isaiah 6:8); a counsellor of kings (Isaiah 37).

Samuel.brief: An elderly man, upright and grave: a firm, clear baritone with a prophet-judge's moral weight. Stern but fatherly, few words, each final.
Samuel.inspiration: Stephen Lang (House of David) and Peter O'Toole (One Night with the King) played him as a stern old seer.
Samuel.scripture: I am old and grayheaded (1 Samuel 12:2); the LORD let none of his words fall to the ground (1 Samuel 3:19).

man in linen above river.brief: A heavenly being of overwhelming presence: a deep, luminous, resonant male voice with great stillness and clarity, as from a vast space. Calm, solemn, kind to the trembling listener.
man in linen above river.inspiration: A vision voice: otherworldly by its stillness, not by effects.
man in linen above river.scripture: The voice of his words like the voice of a multitude (Daniel 10:6).

voice.transcript: At the time appointed he shall return, and come toward the south; but it shall not be as the former, or as the latter.

Eliphaz the Temanite.brief: The eldest of Job's friends, about seventy: a smooth, dignified, slightly patronizing baritone. Courteous, measured, mystical, sure he is wise.
Eliphaz the Temanite.inspiration: The four comforters should be four unmistakable voices: Eliphaz the smooth elder, Bildad the stiff traditionalist, Zophar the blunt one, Elihu the young one.
Eliphaz the Temanite.scripture: With us are both the grayheaded and very aged men (Job 15:10); a vision in the night (Job 4:13).

Joshua.brief: A soldier-leader in his prime, a firm, clear baritone: decisive, courageous, direct. A general's voice that carries across a camp; loyal and devout. 'Joshua (old)' uses this voice, older and slower.
Joshua.inspiration: John Derek played the young Joshua in The Ten Commandments; most portrayals stress strength and courage.
Joshua.scripture: Be strong and of a good courage (Joshua 1:6); as for me and my house, we will serve the LORD (Joshua 24:15).

Joseph.brief: A man from seventeen to his fifties: a clear, earnest tenor-baritone. As the young dreamer, open and a little naive; as Egypt's governor, controlled, commanding and formal, with deep emotion barely held in.
Joseph.inspiration: Ben Affleck voiced him in Joseph: King of Dreams; stage and film Josephs are young and sincere.
Joseph.scripture: He wept aloud (Genesis 45:2); he spoke roughly to his brothers, who did not know him (Genesis 42:7).

Saul.brief: A tall, imposing king in his forties, a strong baritone that grows erratic: proud, jealous, haunted, swinging between charm, rage and despair.
Saul.inspiration: Ali Suliman (House of David) played a magnetic, tormented Saul.
Saul.scripture: From his shoulders and upward he was higher than any of the people (1 Samuel 9:2); an evil spirit troubled him (1 Samuel 16:14).

Rabshakeh.brief: An Assyrian field commander, about fifty: a brash, loud, sneering baritone that bellows across a wall. Propagandist, mocking, arrogant, enjoying the fear he causes.
Rabshakeh.inspiration: A villain's set piece: the siege speech of 2 Kings 18.
Rabshakeh.scripture: Then Rabshakeh stood and cried with a loud voice in the Jews' language (2 Kings 18:28).

Hezekiah, king of Judah.brief: A devout king in his forties, a sincere, gentle baritone; prayerful and earnest, anxious under siege, broken and grateful in sickness and recovery.
Hezekiah, king of Judah.scripture: Hezekiah turned his face toward the wall, and prayed (2 Kings 20:2).

Stephen.brief: A young man in his late twenties, a luminous, fervent tenor. Eloquent, fearless, rising to a prophetic intensity; serene at the end.
Stephen.inspiration: The first martyr's speech is one of the longest in Acts.
Stephen.scripture: They saw his face as it had been the face of an angel (Acts 6:15).

Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon.brief: An emperor in his prime, a booming, imperious bass-baritone, used to absolute obedience; arrogant and volatile, later humbled and awed.
Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon.inspiration: Played as the archetypal tyrant who is brought low.
Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon.scripture: Is not this great Babylon, that I have built? (Daniel 4:30).

Levites.brief: One voice speaking for a group (Levites): a man of about 27. Low pitch, lightly raspy voice, measured, warm in manner. A priest's formality. Natural, unaffected English, clear diction, no caricature.

Elisha.brief: A prophet in his forties, a calmer, compassionate, mellow baritone with steady authority; practical, kind to the poor, occasionally stern.
Elisha.scripture: A holy man of God (2 Kings 4:9).

Elijah.brief: A wild, rough-hewn prophet in his fifties: a fierce, thunderous, gravelly baritone from the desert. Sardonic with false prophets, terrifying to kings, and in the cave, utterly exhausted.
Elijah.inspiration: The archetypal fiery prophet; his successor Elisha must sound distinct.
Elijah.scripture: An hairy man, girt with a girdle of leather (2 Kings 1:8); mocked them, Cry aloud: for he is a god (1 Kings 18:27).

voice.transcript: As the LORD God of Israel liveth, before whom I stand, there shall not be dew nor rain these years, but according to my word.

Yahweh's angel.brief: A messenger who speaks as God himself: a warm, clear, commanding male voice with stillness and light; gentle with the frightened, final in judgment.
Yahweh's angel.inspiration: FCBH casts the angel of the LORD with the actor who plays Jesus (an ancient reading of these appearances). Here he has his own voice unless the owner chooses that tradition (see decisions).
Yahweh's angel.scripture: The angel of the LORD called unto him out of heaven (Genesis 22:11).

Israelites.brief: One voice speaking for a group (Israelites): a person of about 31. Middle-high pitch, reedy voice, measured, warm in manner. Natural, unaffected English, clear diction, no caricature.

And why have ye brought up the congregation of the LORD into this wilderness, that we and our cattle should die there?

voice.transcript: And why have ye brought up the congregation of the LORD into this wilderness, that we and our cattle should die there?

Balaam.brief: A famous foreign seer in his sixties, a theatrical, oily, sonorous baritone; mercenary and ambivalent, grandly poetic in his oracles.
Balaam.inspiration: A conflicted villain with some of the most beautiful oracles in the Torah.
Balaam.scripture: How shall I curse, whom God hath not cursed? (Numbers 23:8).
samples: NUM 22:8
Lodge here this night, and I will bring you word again, as the LORD shall speak unto me:
Balak the son of Zippor, king of Moab, hath sent unto me, saying,
Get you into your land: for the LORD refuseth to give me leave to go with you.
If Balak would give me his house full of silver and gold, I cannot go beyond the word of the LORD my God, to do less or more.
Now therefore, I pray you, tarry ye also here this night, that I may know what the LORD will say unto me more.
Because thou hast mocked me: I would there were a sword in mine hand, for now would I kill thee.
I have sinned; for I knew not that thou stoodest in the way against me: now therefore, if it displease thee, I will get me back again.
Lo, I am come unto thee: have I now any power at all to say any thing? the word that God putteth in my mouth, that shall I speak.
NUM 23:1
Build me here seven altars, and prepare me here seven oxen and seven rams.
NUM 23:3
Stand by thy burnt offering, and I will go: peradventure the LORD will come to meet me: and whatsoever he sheweth me I will tell thee.
NUM 23:4
I have prepared seven altars, and I have offered upon every altar a bullock and a ram.
NUM 23:7
Balak the king of Moab hath brought me from Aram, out of the mountains of the east, saying, Come, curse me Jacob, and come, defy Israel.

voice.transcript: If Balak would give me his house full of silver and gold, I cannot go beyond the word of the LORD my God, to do less or more.

Abraham (Abram).brief: An old man, seventy-five to a hundred and seventy-five: a warm, patient, deep baritone with a nomad chief's hospitality. Gentle authority, faith with a trembling edge; courageous and humble in intercession.
Abraham (Abram).inspiration: George C. Scott (The Bible: In the Beginning), Richard Harris (Abraham, 1994), Jon Voight (The Word of Promise), T. D. Jakes (The Bible Experience).
Abraham (Abram).scripture: I have taken upon me to speak unto the Lord, which am but dust and ashes (Genesis 18:27).
samples: Behold now, I know that thou art a fair woman to look upon:
Say, I pray thee, thou art my sister: that it may be well with me for thy sake; and my soul shall live because of thee.
GEN 13:8
Let there be no strife, I pray thee, between me and thee, and between my herdmen and thy herdmen; for we be brethren.
I have lift up mine hand unto the LORD, the most high God, the possessor of heaven and earth,
Save only that which the young men have eaten, and the portion of the men which went with me, Aner, Eshcol, and Mamre; let them take their portion.
GEN 15:2
Lord GOD, what wilt thou give me, seeing I go childless, and the steward of my house is this Eliezer of Damascus?
GEN 15:3
Behold, to me thou hast given no seed: and, lo, one born in my house is mine heir.
GEN 15:8
Lord GOD, whereby shall I know that I shall inherit it?
GEN 16:6
Behold, thy maid is in thy hand; do to her as it pleaseth thee.
Shall a child be born unto him that is an hundred years old? and shall Sarah, that is ninety years old, bear?
GEN 18:3
My Lord, if now I have found favour in thy sight, pass not away, I pray thee, from thy servant:
GEN 18:4
Let a little water, I pray you, be fetched, and wash your feet, and rest yourselves under the tree:

voice.transcript: Let there be no strife, I pray thee, between me and thee, and between my herdmen and thy herdmen; for we be brethren.

Jonathan.brief: A young prince in his twenties, a warm, bright, loyal baritone; brave, generous, open-hearted, the kindest voice in Saul's court.
Jonathan.inspiration: Always cast as warm and noble.
Jonathan.scripture: The soul of Jonathan was knit with the soul of David (1 Samuel 18:1).
samples: Come, and let us go over to the Philistines’ garrison, that is on the other side.
Behold, we will pass over unto these men, and we will discover ourselves unto them.
If they say thus unto us, Tarry until we come to you; then we will stand still in our place, and will not go up unto them.
But if they say thus, Come up unto us; then we will go up: for the LORD hath delivered them into our hand: and this shall be a sign unto us.
Come up after me: for the LORD hath delivered them into the hand of Israel.
My father hath troubled the land: see, I pray you, how mine eyes have been enlightened, because I tasted a little of this honey.
I did but taste a little honey with the end of the rod that was in mine hand, and, lo, I must die.
Whatsoever thy soul desireth, I will even do it for thee.
Far be it from thee: for if I knew certainly that evil were determined by my father to come upon thee, then would not I tell it thee?
And thou shalt not only while yet I live shew me the kindness of the LORD, that I die not:
Let the LORD even require it at the hand of David’s enemies.
To morrow is the new moon: and thou shalt be missed, because thy seat will be empty.

voice.transcript: My father hath troubled the land: see, I pray you, how mine eyes have been enlightened, because I tasted a little of this honey.

Wisdom.brief: Wisdom personified, a woman of radiant maturity: a clear, ringing, joyful mezzo voice calling in the streets. Commanding, generous, delighted, ancient and young at once.
Wisdom.inspiration: Proverbs makes Wisdom a woman; productions give her a luminous, confident voice.
Wisdom.scripture: Doth not wisdom cry? (Proverbs 8:1); I was daily his delight, rejoicing always before him (Proverbs 8:30).
samples: PRO 1:22
How long, ye simple ones, will ye love simplicity? and the scorners delight in their scorning, and fools hate knowledge?
PRO 1:23
Turn you at my reproof: behold, I will pour out my spirit unto you, I will make known my words unto you.
PRO 1:24
Because I have called, and ye refused; I have stretched out my hand, and no man regarded;
PRO 1:25
But ye have set at nought all my counsel, and would none of my reproof:
PRO 1:26
I also will laugh at your calamity; I will mock when your fear cometh;
PRO 1:27
When your fear cometh as desolation, and your destruction cometh as a whirlwind; when distress and anguish cometh upon you.
PRO 1:28
Then shall they call upon me, but I will not answer; they shall seek me early, but they shall not find me:
PRO 1:29
For that they hated knowledge, and did not choose the fear of the LORD:
PRO 1:30
They would none of my counsel: they despised all my reproof.
PRO 1:31
Therefore shall they eat of the fruit of their own way, and be filled with their own devices.
PRO 1:32
For the turning away of the simple shall slay them, and the prosperity of fools shall destroy them.
PRO 1:33
But whoso hearkeneth unto me shall dwell safely, and shall be quiet from fear of evil.

voice.transcript: When your fear cometh as desolation, and your destruction cometh as a whirlwind; when distress and anguish cometh upon you.

John the Baptist.brief: A wilderness ascetic in his early thirties: a raw, fiery, booming outdoor voice, rough and intense. Uncompromising and urgent, humble before the one he heralds.
John the Baptist.inspiration: Charlton Heston (The Greatest Story Ever Told), Robert Ryan (King of Kings, 1961), Michael York (Jesus of Nazareth).
John the Baptist.scripture: The voice of one crying in the wilderness (Matthew 3:3); O generation of vipers (Matthew 3:7).
samples: MAT 3:2
And saying, Repent ye: for the kingdom of heaven is at hand.
MAT 3:7
O generation of vipers, who hath warned you to flee from the wrath to come?
MAT 3:8
Bring forth therefore fruits meet for repentance:
MAT 3:14
I have need to be baptized of thee, and comest thou to me?
MRK 1:7
There cometh one mightier than I after me, the latchet of whose shoes I am not worthy to stoop down and unloose.
MRK 1:8
I indeed have baptized you with water: but he shall baptize you with the Holy Ghost.
MRK 6:18
It is not lawful for thee to have thy brother’s wife.
LUK 3:7
O generation of vipers, who hath warned you to flee from the wrath to come?
LUK 3:11
He that hath two coats, let him impart to him that hath none; and he that hath meat, let him do likewise.
LUK 3:13
Exact no more than that which is appointed you.
LUK 3:14
Do violence to no man, neither accuse any falsely; and be content with your wages.
LUK 7:19
Art thou he that should come? or look we for another?

voice.transcript: There cometh one mightier than I after me, the latchet of whose shoes I am not worthy to stoop down and unloose.

Zophar the Naamathite.brief: A man in his fifties, a harsh, abrupt, coarse baritone. Impatient, blunt to the point of rudeness, quick to condemn.
Zophar the Naamathite.scripture: Should a man full of talk be justified? (Job 11:2).
samples: JOB 11:2
Should not the multitude of words be answered? and should a man full of talk be justified?
JOB 11:3
Should thy lies make men hold their peace? and when thou mockest, shall no man make thee ashamed?
JOB 11:4
For thou hast said, My doctrine is pure, and I am clean in thine eyes.
JOB 11:5
But oh that God would speak, and open his lips against thee;
JOB 11:7
Canst thou by searching find out God? canst thou find out the Almighty unto perfection?
JOB 11:8
It is as high as heaven; what canst thou do? deeper than hell; what canst thou know?
JOB 11:9
The measure thereof is longer than the earth, and broader than the sea.
If he cut off, and shut up, or gather together, then who can hinder him?
For he knoweth vain men: he seeth wickedness also; will he not then consider it?
For vain man would be wise, though man be born like a wild ass’s colt.
If thou prepare thine heart, and stretch out thine hands toward him;
If iniquity be in thine hand, put it far away, and let not wickedness dwell in thy tabernacles.

voice.transcript: Should thy lies make men hold their peace? and when thou mockest, shall no man make thee ashamed?

Gabriel.brief: An archangel: a radiant, clear, warm tenor with serene, awe-inspiring authority. Gentle with the afraid, joyful in announcement.
Gabriel.inspiration: Classic annunciation scenes give him a luminous, kind voice.
Gabriel.scripture: I am Gabriel, that stand in the presence of God (Luke 1:19); Fear not, Mary (Luke 1:30).
samples: DAN 8:17
Understand, O son of man: for at the time of the end shall be the vision.
DAN 8:19
Behold, I will make thee know what shall be in the last end of the indignation: for at the time appointed the end shall be.
DAN 8:20
The ram which thou sawest having two horns are the kings of Media and Persia.
DAN 8:21
And the rough goat is the king of Grecia: and the great horn that is between his eyes is the first king.
DAN 8:22
Now that being broken, whereas four stood up for it, four kingdoms shall stand up out of the nation, but not in his power.
DAN 8:26
And the vision of the evening and the morning which was told is true: wherefore shut thou up the vision; for it shall be for many days.
DAN 9:22
O Daniel, I am now come forth to give thee skill and understanding.
LUK 1:13
Fear not, Zacharias: for thy prayer is heard; and thy wife Elisabeth shall bear thee a son, and thou shalt call his name John.
LUK 1:14
And thou shalt have joy and gladness; and many shall rejoice at his birth.
LUK 1:16
And many of the children of Israel shall he turn to the Lord their God.
LUK 1:19
I am Gabriel, that stand in the presence of God; and am sent to speak unto thee, and to shew thee these glad tidings.
LUK 1:28
Hail, thou that art highly favoured, the Lord is with thee: blessed art thou among women.

voice.transcript: Now that being broken, whereas four stood up for it, four kingdoms shall stand up out of the nation, but not in his power.

Joab.brief: A hard-bitten general in his fifties, a gravelly, clipped, pragmatic baritone; ruthless and loyal, sardonic, a soldier's bluntness.
Joab.inspiration: The archetypal hard man of David's court.
Joab.scripture: Joab the son of Zeruiah (2 Samuel 2:13).
samples: As God liveth, unless thou hadst spoken, surely then in the morning the people had gone up every one from following his brother.
What hast thou done? behold, Abner came unto thee; why is it that thou hast sent him away, and he is quite gone?
Thou knowest Abner the son of Ner, that he came to deceive thee, and to know thy going out and thy coming in, and to know all that thou doest.
If the Syrians be too strong for me, then thou shalt help me: but if the children of Ammon be too strong for thee, then I will come and help thee.
Be of good courage, and let us play the men for our people, and for the cities of our God: and the LORD do that which seemeth him good.
When thou hast made an end of telling the matters of the war unto the king,
I have fought against Rabbah, and have taken the city of waters.
Now therefore gather the rest of the people together, and encamp against the city, and take it: lest I take the city, and it be called after my name.
And come to the king, and speak on this manner unto him.
To day thy servant knoweth that I have found grace in thy sight, my lord, O king, in that the king hath fulfilled the request of his servant.
Wherefore have thy servants set my field on fire?
And, behold, thou sawest him, and why didst thou not smite him there to the ground? and I would have given thee ten shekels of silver, and a girdle.

voice.transcript: As God liveth, unless thou hadst spoken, surely then in the morning the people had gone up every one from following his brother.

Judah.brief: A rugged man in his forties, a strong, rough baritone that grows in dignity: brash among his brothers, eloquent and broken when pleading for Benjamin.
Judah.inspiration: Mark Hamill voiced him in Joseph: King of Dreams.
Judah.scripture: His plea of Genesis 44:18-34 is among the most moving speeches in Genesis.
samples: What profit is it if we slay our brother, and conceal his blood?
Come, and let us sell him to the Ishmeelites, and let not our hand be upon him; for he is our brother and our flesh.
GEN 38:8
Go in unto thy brother’s wife, and marry her, and raise up seed to thy brother.
Remain a widow at thy father’s house, till Shelah my son be grown:
Lest peradventure he die also, as his brethren did.
Go to, I pray thee, let me come in unto thee;
Let her take it to her, lest we be shamed: behold, I sent this kid, and thou hast not found her.
She hath been more righteous than I; because that I gave her not to Shelah my son.
GEN 43:3
The man did solemnly protest unto us, saying, Ye shall not see my face, except your brother be with you.
GEN 43:4
If thou wilt send our brother with us, we will go down and buy thee food:
GEN 43:5
But if thou wilt not send him, we will not go down: for the man said unto us, Ye shall not see my face, except your brother be with you.
GEN 43:8
Send the lad with me, and we will arise and go; that we may live, and not die, both we, and thou, and also our little ones.

voice.transcript: Send the lad with me, and we will arise and go; that we may live, and not die, both we, and thou, and also our little ones.

Bildad the Shuhite.brief: A man in his sixties, a dry, stiff, moralizing tenor-baritone. Brisk and formal; recites tradition like a lecturer; little warmth.
Bildad the Shuhite.inspiration: Played as the friend who argues from the fathers.
Bildad the Shuhite.scripture: Enquire, I pray thee, of the former age (Job 8:8).
samples: JOB 8:2
How long wilt thou speak these things? and how long shall the words of thy mouth be like a strong wind?
JOB 8:3
Doth God pervert judgment? or doth the Almighty pervert justice?
JOB 8:4
If thy children have sinned against him, and he have cast them away for their transgression;
JOB 8:5
If thou wouldest seek unto God betimes, and make thy supplication to the Almighty;
JOB 8:6
If thou wert pure and upright; surely now he would awake for thee, and make the habitation of thy righteousness prosperous.
JOB 8:7
Though thy beginning was small, yet thy latter end should greatly increase.
JOB 8:8
For enquire, I pray thee, of the former age, and prepare thyself to the search of their fathers:
JOB 8:9
(For we are but of yesterday, and know nothing, because our days upon earth are a shadow:)
JOB 8:10
Shall not they teach thee, and tell thee, and utter words out of their heart?
JOB 8:11
Can the rush grow up without mire? can the flag grow without water?
JOB 8:12
Whilst it is yet in his greenness, and not cut down, it withereth before any other herb.
JOB 8:13
So are the paths of all that forget God; and the hypocrite’s hope shall perish:

voice.transcript: If thou wert pure and upright; surely now he would awake for thee, and make the habitation of thy righteousness prosperous.

Deborah/Barak.brief: Shared by Deborah and Barak; led by Deborah's voice.
Deborah/Barak.inspiration: Joan Allen (The Word of Promise) as Deborah.
Deborah/Barak.scripture: Judges 5, the Song of Deborah, is sung by both.
samples: JDG 5:2
Praise ye the LORD for the avenging of Israel, when the people willingly offered themselves.
JDG 5:3
Hear, O ye kings; give ear, O ye princes; I, even I, will sing unto the LORD; I will sing praise to the LORD God of Israel.
JDG 5:5
The mountains melted from before the LORD, even that Sinai from before the LORD God of Israel.
JDG 5:6
In the days of Shamgar the son of Anath, in the days of Jael, the highways were unoccupied, and the travellers walked through byways.
JDG 5:7
The inhabitants of the villages ceased, they ceased in Israel, until that I Deborah arose, that I arose a mother in Israel.
JDG 5:8
They chose new gods; then was war in the gates: was there a shield or spear seen among forty thousand in Israel?
JDG 5:9
My heart is toward the governors of Israel, that offered themselves willingly among the people. Bless ye the LORD.
JDG 5:10
Speak, ye that ride on white asses, ye that sit in judgment, and walk by the way.
JDG 5:12
Awake, awake, Deborah: awake, awake, utter a song: arise, Barak, and lead thy captivity captive, thou son of Abinoam.
JDG 5:13
Then he made him that remaineth have dominion over the nobles among the people: the LORD made me have dominion over the mighty.
JDG 5:16
Why abodest thou among the sheepfolds, to hear the bleatings of the flocks? For the divisions of Reuben there were great searchings of heart.
JDG 5:17
Gilead abode beyond Jordan: and why did Dan remain in ships? Asher continued on the sea shore, and abode in his breaches.

Abraham's chief servant.brief: An elderly steward, about sixty-five: a careful, humble, faithful baritone; a natural storyteller retelling his errand with quiet wonder.
Abraham's chief servant.inspiration: Trusted servant of a great house.
Abraham's chief servant.scripture: The eldest servant of his house, that ruled over all that he had (Genesis 24:2).
samples: GEN 24:5
Peradventure the woman will not be willing to follow me unto this land: must I needs bring thy son again unto the land from whence thou camest?
O LORD God of my master Abraham, I pray thee, send me good speed this day, and shew kindness unto my master Abraham.
Behold, I stand here by the well of water; and the daughters of the men of the city come out to draw water:
Let me, I pray thee, drink a little water of thy pitcher.
Whose daughter art thou? tell me, I pray thee: is there room in thy father’s house for us to lodge in?
I will not eat, until I have told mine errand.
And Sarah my master’s wife bare a son to my master when she was old: and unto him hath he given all that he hath.
And my master made me swear, saying, Thou shalt not take a wife to my son of the daughters of the Canaanites, in whose land I dwell:
But thou shalt go unto my father’s house, and to my kindred, and take a wife unto my son.
And I said unto my master, Peradventure the woman will not follow me.
Then shalt thou be clear from this my oath, when thou comest to my kindred; and if they give not thee one, thou shalt be clear from my oath.
And I came this day unto the well, and said, O LORD God of my master Abraham, if now thou do prosper my way which I go:

voice.transcript: And I came this day unto the well, and said, O LORD God of my master Abraham, if now thou do prosper my way which I go:

disciples.brief: One voice speaking for a group (disciples): a man of about 33. Middle pitch, lightly raspy voice, quick and urgent, earnest in manner. Natural, unaffected English, clear diction, no caricature.
samples: MAT 8:27
What manner of man is this, that even the winds and the sea obey him!
Why speakest thou unto them in parables?
Declare unto us the parable of the tares of the field.
This is a desert place, and the time is now past; send the multitude away, that they may go into the villages, and buy themselves victuals.
Knowest thou that the Pharisees were offended, after they heard this saying?
Whence should we have so much bread in the wilderness, as to fill so great a multitude?
Some say that thou art John the Baptist: some, Elias; and others, Jeremias, or one of the prophets.
MAT 18:1
Who is the greatest in the kingdom of heaven?
If the case of the man be so with his wife, it is not good to marry.
MAT 26:9
For this ointment might have been sold for much, and given to the poor.
MRK 4:41
What manner of man is this, that even the wind and the sea obey him?
MRK 5:31
Thou seest the multitude thronging thee, and sayest thou, Who touched me?

voice.transcript: This is a desert place, and the time is now past; send the multitude away, that they may go into the villages, and buy themselves victuals.

Ahijah the prophet.brief: A very old, blind prophet: a thin, grave, solemn voice with a seer's certainty.
Ahijah the prophet.scripture: Ahijah could not see; for his eyes were set by reason of his age (1 Kings 14:4).
samples: (But he shall have one tribe for my servant David’s sake, and for Jerusalem’s sake, the city which I have chosen out of all the tribes of Israel:)
But I will take the kingdom out of his son’s hand, and will give it unto thee, even ten tribes.
And I will take thee, and thou shalt reign according to all that thy soul desireth, and shalt be king over Israel.
And I will for this afflict the seed of David, but not for ever.
Come in, thou wife of Jeroboam; why feignest thou thyself to be another? for I am sent to thee with heavy tidings.
Go, tell Jeroboam, Thus saith the LORD God of Israel, Forasmuch as I exalted thee from among the people, and made thee prince over my people Israel,
Arise thou therefore, get thee to thine own house: and when thy feet enter into the city, the child shall die.
Moreover the LORD shall raise him up a king over Israel, who shall cut off the house of Jeroboam that day: but what? even now.
And he shall give Israel up because of the sins of Jeroboam, who did sin, and who made Israel to sin.

voice.transcript: And I will take thee, and thou shalt reign according to all that thy soul desireth, and shalt be king over Israel.

Ahab, king of Israel.brief: A king in his forties, a blustering, petulant, sulky baritone; vain, weak-willed, easily led, occasionally shrewd.
Ahab, king of Israel.scripture: He laid him down upon his bed, and turned away his face, and would eat no bread (1 Kings 21:4).
samples: My lord, O king, according to thy saying, I am thine, and all that I have.
Tell my lord the king, All that thou didst send for to thy servant at the first I will do: but this thing I may not do.
Tell him, Let not him that girdeth on his harness boast himself as he that putteth it off.
Then said Ahab, I will send thee away with this covenant.
So shall thy judgment be; thyself hast decided it.
Know ye that Ramoth in Gilead is ours, and we be still, and take it not out of the hand of the king of Syria?
Wilt thou go with me to battle to Ramoth-gilead?
Shall I go against Ramoth-gilead to battle, or shall I forbear?
Micaiah, shall we go against Ramoth-gilead to battle, or shall we forbear?
How many times shall I adjure thee that thou tell me nothing but that which is true in the name of the LORD?
Did I not tell thee that he would prophesy no good concerning me, but evil?
Take Micaiah, and carry him back unto Amon the governor of the city, and to Joash the king’s son;

voice.transcript: Tell my lord the king, All that thou didst send for to thy servant at the first I will do: but this thing I may not do.

Artaxerxes, king of Persia.brief: A Persian emperor, about forty: a formal, polished, unhurried voice of decrees, cultured and reserved.
samples: EZR 4:18
The letter which ye sent unto us hath been plainly read before me.
EZR 4:21
Give ye now commandment to cause these men to cease, and that this city be not builded, until another commandment shall be given from me.
EZR 4:22
Take heed now that ye fail not to do this: why should damage grow to the hurt of the kings?
EZR 7:12
Artaxerxes, king of kings, unto Ezra the priest, a scribe of the law of the God of heaven, perfect peace, and at such a time.
EZR 7:15
And to carry the silver and gold, which the king and his counsellors have freely offered unto the God of Israel, whose habitation is in Jerusalem,
EZR 7:18
And whatsoever shall seem good to thee, and to thy brethren, to do with the rest of the silver and the gold, that do after the will of your God.
EZR 7:19
The vessels also that are given thee for the service of the house of thy God, those deliver thou before the God of Jerusalem.
EZR 7:20
And whatsoever more shall be needful for the house of thy God, which thou shalt have occasion to bestow, bestow it out of the king’s treasure house.
NEH 2:2
Why is thy countenance sad, seeing thou art not sick? this is nothing else but sorrow of heart.
NEH 2:6
For how long shall thy journey be? and when wilt thou return?

voice.transcript: The vessels also that are given thee for the service of the house of thy God, those deliver thou before the God of Jerusalem.

Nathan.brief: A court prophet in his sixties: a wise, tactful, calm baritone that tells a story gently, then cuts like a blade.
Nathan.inspiration: Raymond Massey played him in David and Bathsheba.
samples: Go, do all that is in thine heart; for the LORD is with thee.
There were two men in one city; the one rich, and the other poor.
The rich man had exceeding many flocks and herds:
Thou art the man. Thus saith the LORD God of Israel, I anointed thee king over Israel, and I delivered thee out of the hand of Saul;
For thou didst it secretly: but I will do this thing before all Israel, and before the sun.
The LORD also hath put away thy sin; thou shalt not die.
Hast thou not heard that Adonijah the son of Haggith doth reign, and David our lord knoweth it not?
Now therefore come, let me, I pray thee, give thee counsel, that thou mayest save thine own life, and the life of thy son Solomon.
Behold, while thou yet talkest there with the king, I also will come in after thee, and confirm thy words.
My lord, O king, hast thou said, Adonijah shall reign after me, and he shall sit upon my throne?
But me, even me thy servant, and Zadok the priest, and Benaiah the son of Jehoiada, and thy servant Solomon, hath he not called.
Is this thing done by my lord the king, and thou hast not shewed it unto thy servant, who should sit on the throne of my lord the king after him?

voice.transcript: Now therefore come, let me, I pray thee, give thee counsel, that thou mayest save thine own life, and the life of thy son Solomon.

Pharaoh (3rd).brief: Egypt's god-king in his forties: a cold, imperious, contemptuous baritone, aristocratic and hardening into fury; never begs, until he does.
Pharaoh (3rd).inspiration: Yul Brynner's Rameses (The Ten Commandments), Ralph Fiennes (The Prince of Egypt), Joel Edgerton (Exodus: Gods and Kings).
Pharaoh (3rd).scripture: Who is the LORD, that I should obey his voice? (Exodus 5:2).
samples: EXO 1:9
Behold, the people of the children of Israel are more and mightier than we:
EXO 1:18
Why have ye done this thing, and have saved the men children alive?
EXO 1:22
